title: A content-addressed store for timetables

blocks.text: A bus operator keeps every timetable version its scheduling service has used, in a bucket of files (`Store.files`, a dict from name to bytes, stands in for it). Each scenario, such as `"winter"`, has a chain of versions; an auditor must be able to fetch the exact timetable behind any run and know it was not changed since.
In `timetables.py`, write `Store.put(doc, scenario)` and `Store.get(key)`. `canonical(doc)` is written.

items: `put` stores the timetable's canonical bytes under their SHA-256 hex digest and returns the digest. A name that is already in `files` is never written again.

`put` appends `{"scenario", "version", "digest", "parent"}` to `log` when the content differs from that scenario's latest version: versions count from 1 within each scenario, and `parent` is the digest of the scenario's previous version (`None` for the first). Sending the scenario's latest content again adds nothing; going back to older content is a new version.
`get(key)` returns the stored timetable as a dict, or `None` when there is no such file or its bytes no longer hash to `key`.

cases.says: a timetable is stored under the digest of its canonical bytes, read back unchanged, and logged as version 1 with no parent
the same content sent twice, keys in another order, is one file and one version
returning to an earlier timetable is a new version whose parent is the one before it, and no new file
a stored file whose bytes were edited is refused on read
each scenario numbers its own versions and has its own parents
putting the same content again never rewrites its file, so an edit stays visible

origin.section: A Snapshot Is Stored Once Under Its Digest and Checked Again on Every Read

concepts: a store that names each file by its digest, writes it once, logs versions with their parents per scenario, and re-hashes on every read
